question: A 28-year-old man presents with bloody diarrhoea and right hypochondriac pain. Ultrasound confirms an amoebic liver abscess. Which pharmacotherapy plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Metronidazole 750 mg TDS × 10 days followed by diloxanide furoate 500 mg TDS × 10 days

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For invasive amoebiasis (amoebic liver abscess), metronidazole is the tissue amoebicide of choice. It must be followed by a luminal amoebicide (diloxanide furoate or paromomycin) to eradicate intestinal cysts and prevent relapse.

answers.text: Diloxanide furoate alone for 10 days, as it targets both tissue and luminal stages

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Diloxanide furoate is a luminal amoebicide only — it does not achieve adequate tissue concentrations to treat invasive disease or liver abscess.

answers.text: Metronidazole alone for 14 days without a follow-up luminal agent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Metronidazole treats tissue-stage amoebiasis but does not reliably eradicate luminal cysts. Without a luminal agent follow-up, relapse rates are high.

answers.text: Chloroquine 600 mg base loading dose followed by metronidazole

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chloroquine is sometimes used as a second-line agent for amoebic liver abscess when metronidazole fails, but it is not part of first-line treatment and does not replace metronidazole.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Amoebiasis Pharmacotherapy block. Invasive disease requires a tissue amoebicide (metronidazole/tinidazole) followed by a luminal agent to eliminate intestinal carriage.
Excellent. The two-drug sequential strategy — metronidazole (tissue) then diloxanide furoate (luminal) — is the standard for invasive amoebiasis.
